newsitem.title: URUGUAY: Uruguay releases two Peruvian guerrilla suspects.
newsitem.headline: Uruguay releases two Peruvian guerrilla suspects.

text.p: The Uruguayan government on Tuesday night confirmed the release of two alleged members of the Peruvian Marxist guerrilla group that is holding 105 hostages at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.
Officials denied the release of the two Peruvians arrested in Uruguay a year ago had helped secure the freeing by the rebels of Uruguayan ambassador Tabare Bocalandro later on Tuesday in Lima.
"There were no negotiations. This is just a coincidence," Foreign Minister Alvaro Ramos told reporters. "The court ruling was due in the case of the Peruvians, and proceedings finished today."

But a well-placed government source said a deal had been cut with the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) and the two Peruvians, who were appealing against their extradition to Peru, had been swapped for the ambassador.
"This was an exchange," the senior government aide told Reuters.
Luis Alberto Samaniego and Silvia Gora Rivero, presumed to be MRTA militants, were released after a Uruguayan appeals courts overturned an earlier court ruling authorising Peru's extradition request.
The couple were arrested a year ago after entered Uruguay with false Bolivian documents.
A Uruguayan court initially granted their extradition in March, but Samaniego and Gora appealed the ruling on grounds they had no guarantees of a fair trial in Peru.

Peruvians were suspected of taken part in the 1995 kidnapping of Bolivian businessman and former government official, Samuel Doria Medina, who was freed a month and a half later for a $1.2 million ransom.
Samaniego and Gora were surprised by their sudden release.
"The decision to free us took us by surprise. Since May the court had done nothing," Samaniego told Uruguay's Channel Four.
His lawyer said the release was directly related to the freeing of the Uruguayan ambassador in Lima.
"You don't have to be a mind-reader to presume that the ambassador called President (Julio) Sanguinetti trying to speed up a solution," the lawyer, Gustavo Puig, told Reuters.
